Hi Dylan,

Thanks for taking our DPA annex review. A few follow-ups from our side: we classify certain 'telemetry-derived' identifiers as PII when they can be linked back to an end user after enrichment (device fingerprint + account_id). The security and legal teams need:

- A single-page dataflow diagram showing where telemetry is ingested, enriched, and where PII becomes persistently stored or exported.
- An authorization matrix listing roles that can read raw telemetry, enriched identifiers, and any downstream exports to subprocessors.
- Confirmation of key custody (KMS vs. customer-managed) for telemetry manifests and logs.

Can you provide an initial diagram and a draft authz matrix by EOD Friday? Also flag any subprocessors that will see telemetry-derived PII in the processing path.

Thanks,

Hi Ava,

Thanks — we can put this together. Attached are two artifacts to start the conversation: a draft dataflow PDF (redwood_dpa_dataflow_v1.pdf) and a draft authorization matrix CSV (authz_matrix_draft_v1.csv). High-level notes below:

- Telemetry ingestion: ephemeral collectors forward events to our ingestion cluster. Raw telemetry is retained in hot storage for 7 days for processing, then moved to cold-tier logs for 90 days by default (configurable per-customer).
- Enrichment: account_id joins and fingerprinting happen in the enrichment layer; at the point of enrichment an identifier becomes "telemetry-derived PII" if it's attached to account_id or other direct identifier.
- Persistent storage: only pseudonymized aggregates are persisted in model training stores; customer-configured retention controls govern export windows.
- KMS custody: customer-seeded KMS keys protect exported artifacts; operational logs are encrypted with Redwood-managed keys (we can switch to BYOK under Private deployments).

Open items we want your feedback on: the export gating logic (can a subprocessor receive raw enriched identifiers, or only pseudonymized aggregates?) and whether your legal team needs per-field redaction exhibited in the matrix.

I looped in Marissa for routing and Connor for KMS/custody specifics. We can iterate quickly — propose a 30-minute walkthrough Thursday.

Thanks,

Dylan Brooks

2) Authorization matrix: we should split roles into operational (SRE, Ingest Ops), product (Feature Team), and legal/compliance viewers. For each role indicate: read_raw_telemetry, read_enriched_identifiers, export_to_subprocessor, and ability_to_request_key_rotation.

Note: two analytics partners can receive only aggregated outputs; no partner gets raw enriched identifiers in our hosted offering unless the customer explicitly requests a dedicated export and signs a subprocessor appendix.
